extra_misconceptions.fact: Dewey Decimal numbers are read digit by digit after the decimal point, so 598.12 is shelved before 598.2 on the shelf.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dewey Decimal call numbers are shelved by whole-number value after the decimal point, placing 598.12 after 598.2.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Subject searches match standardized controlled vocabulary tags, whereas keyword searches scan titles and notes for any matching word.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Keyword searches and subject heading searches in a computerized library catalog return the exact same list of books.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most public libraries shelve general fiction alphabetically by the author's last name rather than by numeric subject codes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Fiction novels in a public library are arranged numerically by Dewey Decimal class numbers just like nonfiction books.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Non-circulating reference materials must remain inside the library building so all patrons have immediate access to them.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Reference section encyclopedias and atlases can be checked out for home reading using a standard library card.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a Dewey Decimal shelf search when you read the cutter numbers after the decimal point as whole numbers?
Which catalog index field retrieves all holdings about civil rights regardless of the exact words used in a book title?
Where on a library book spine do you find the author cutter code that orders books sharing the same subject number?
Under what condition does an online catalog list a book as owned by the branch while the shelf location remains empty?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Front-matter lists only show titles printed before that specific edition went to press and often omit works from other publishers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The front flyleaf list titled Also by This Author in an older paperback includes every book the writer ever published.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bestseller lists rank commercial retail sales volume, whereas library award committees judge literary merit and youth appeal.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Bestseller lists and library award lists like the Newbery or Printz medals use the same selection criteria.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many prolific authors co-author franchise series with partners whose names appear in smaller print or catalog credits.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every book bearing a famous novelist's name on the cover was written solely by that author without a co-writer.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Authors frequently write prequels years after the original book, making internal timeline order different from publication dates.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Reading a book series in publication order is always identical to reading the story in internal chronological order.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to an author bibliography search if the writer published several novels under a pen name or pseudonym?
Which publication detail in a series bibliography tells you whether to read books in internal chronological or release order?
Where in a library catalog record can you click to view every title linked to the same verified author authority record?
Under what condition does an annual best-books list serve a reader better than an all-time literary classics list?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Effective book reviews evaluate theme, style, and audience fit while avoiding spoilers that ruin the ending for future readers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A strong book review should retell every major plot twist and reveal the ending so the counselor knows you finished it.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Biographies document verifiable facts supported by sources, whereas historical fiction invents scenes and dialogue around history.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Historical fiction and biography belong to the same literary genre because both portray real historical figures and eras.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Poetry relies on meter, imagery, and line breaks that reward slow rereading and aloud recitation rather than rapid page turning.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Poetry collections must be read straight through at the same speed as a prose novel to count toward reading logs.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Recording impressions right after each reading session preserves specific reactions and questions that fade once the book ends.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Waiting until you finish all four books to write every reading journal entry captures the same insights as logging daily.

extra_socratic_questions: What distinguishes a critical book review that evaluates evidence and pacing from a simple plot summary with spoilers?
Which textual evidence in a biography confirms the author relied on primary sources rather than invented dialogue?
What log entries allow a Scout to track how a character or argument develops across chapters during a reading journal?
Under what condition would you recommend a technically dense nonfiction book to a specific audience despite slow pacing?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Requirement 4 explicitly excludes merit badge pamphlets, requiring an independent how-to book or magazine for your project.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A Scouting merit badge pamphlet counts as the instructional nonfiction book or magazine required to complete Requirement 4.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Reading the complete procedure and bill of materials first prevents mid-project hazards, missing tools, and timing mistakes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: You can begin cutting wood or heating ingredients as soon as you read Step 1 of a project without reading to the end.

extra_misconceptions.fact: You must secure permission from both your parent or guardian and your counselor before starting the hands-on project.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Parent and counselor permission can be obtained after building the project from the instructional book at home.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Technical diagrams often contain critical dimensions, orientation arrows, and assembly tolerances omitted from the body text.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Diagrams and callout figures in technical manuals are decorative illustrations that repeat the exact text in the paragraphs.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to start a woodworking or chemistry project before reading the entire instructional sequence through once?
Which section of an instructional manual tells you the exact tool sizes and safety gear required before cutting materials?
What happens to a project outcome when a builder substitutes metric and imperial measurements listed in a manual diagram?
Under what condition must you stop an instructional project and consult your parent or counselor before proceeding further?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Two sites syndicating the same wire report represent a single source; choose independent formats or publications for comparison.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Reading two websites that repost the same wire-service story satisfies the spirit of comparing two current-event sources.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Newspapers publish both verified news reporting and labeled op-ed columns that express the personal viewpoint of the writer.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every article published inside a reputable newspaper is an objective news report rather than a persuasive opinion piece.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Search algorithms rank pages by popularity and keyword optimization, so readers must still verify citations and author expertise.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Top search engine results about a social or environmental topic are ranked by factual accuracy and peer review.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Requirement 5 explicitly requires parent or guardian permission before using the internet as one of your reading sources.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Scouts can research internet sources for Requirement 5 independently without checking in with a parent or guardian first.

extra_socratic_questions: Which publication markers distinguish a factual news report from an opinion editorial in a newspaper or online outlet?
What happens to your understanding of an environmental issue when you compare a daily news article with a field manual?
Where in an online article can you verify the author's credentials, primary data sources, and date of publication?
Under what condition does an older printed magazine article give misleading information about a rapidly changing topic?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Requirement 6 states that you must choose one activity option and devote at least four hours of service to that single activity.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: You can split the four required service hours across two different options, such as two hours shelving and two hours reading.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Effective oral reading requires a measured pace, clear articulation, and regular pauses to check listener comfort and fatigue.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Reading aloud to a patient in an extended-care facility works best when you read as fast as you read silently to yourself.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Donated books must be sorted for target reading level and inspected to remove moldy, torn, or water-damaged copies before delivery.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Book drive volunteers should pack every donated volume into community distribution boxes regardless of condition or age appropriateness.

extra_misconceptions.fact: You must obtain permission from both your counselor and your parent or guardian before beginning your four literacy service hours.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Volunteer hours completed at a school library for another class requirement automatically count without prior counselor approval.

extra_socratic_questions: What vocal adjustments help a listener with visual impairment follow scene changes and dialogue when you read aloud?
Why is it important to pre-read a storybook before reading it aloud to young children at a library or camp session?
What details must your service log record across sessions to verify four hours of approved literacy volunteer work?
Where must a Scout stand and hold an illustrated picture book so an entire circle of younger children can see the pages?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Libraries employ pages, technicians, and ALA-accredited master's-level librarians who have distinct credentials and pay scales.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every staff member working behind a public library desk holds the same job title and Master of Library Science degree.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Technical writers, paralegals, intelligence analysts, medical coders, and archivists all rely heavily on advanced reading skills.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Careers centered on reading skills are limited to classroom English teachers, book editors, and public librarians.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Entering the field often includes licensing exam fees, unpaid practicum hours, background checks, and continuing education costs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: University tuition is the only out-of-pocket expense required to enter a certified reading or library profession.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Organizations still require skilled human editors and information specialists to verify accuracy, legal compliance, and clarity.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Digital publishing and artificial intelligence tools have eliminated the need for human editors and technical proofreaders.

extra_socratic_questions: Which credential separates a professional public or academic librarian from a paraprofessional library circulation technician?
What happens to the net financial return of a reading career when you compare starting salary against degree tuition costs?
Where can a Scout find verified national data on employment outlook and median starting pay for editors or archivists?
Under what condition does a state require a specialist certification in addition to a bachelor's degree for reading teachers?
